title: Tentmakers (Acts 18)
hook: Priscilla and Aquila work with Paul and teach Apollos more perfectly

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Areopagus in Athens, and the altar to the unknown God. Your line was in him we live.

Picture a workshop in Corinth, a busy port city. Leather and canvas, needles, awls, the smell of hides. Three people bent over their work, talking while they stitch. One of them is the Apostle Paul. It's easy to picture Paul only preaching to crowds or writing letters, and he did both. But much of his week, he was working with his hands to pay his own way. Luke tells us exactly what the job was: they were tentmakers.
screen: `A WORKSHOP IN CORINTH.` → `PAUL WITH A NEEDLE.` → `THEY WERE TENTMAKERS.`

segments.voice: The other two are a married couple, Aquila and Priscilla, Jews who had recently come from Rome, because the emperor Claudius had ordered Jews to leave the city. Paul stays with them, the text says, because they shared his trade. He works with them through the week, and on the Sabbath he speaks in the synagogue. The Greek word is skenopoioi, tent makers, though it may have meant leatherworkers more broadly. In a letter probably written from Corinth, Paul reminds the Thessalonians that he worked night and day so as not to be a burden to anyone. Now jump ahead. Priscilla and Aquila move with Paul to Ephesus, and a man named Apollos arrives from Alexandria: eloquent, mighty in the scriptures, on fire, teaching accurately about Jesus. But he knows only the baptism of John. So what do Priscilla and Aquila do? They don't correct him in front of everyone. In the Douay-Rheims, they "took him to them, and expounded to him the way of the Lord more diligently." The Greek means more exactly; older English Bibles put it as more perfectly, today's line. They take him aside, probably to their home, maybe their workshop, and fill in what he's missing. Then they send him on with letters of recommendation, and Apollos becomes a great help to the believers in Achaia. One more thing: more than once, Luke names Priscilla first. Many scholars think that means she was the better known of the two, maybe the leading teacher. Two tentmakers quietly shaped a preacher Paul later names in the same breath as himself and Peter. Catholics honor them as saints.
screen: `AQUILA AND PRISCILLA, FROM ROME.` · `PAUL WORKS WITH HIS HANDS.` · `APOLLOS, ELOQUENT, BUT MISSING SOMETHING.` · `THEY TOOK HIM ASIDE.` · then, large: `MORE PERFECTLY.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who is good at something, enthusiastic, maybe a little ahead of what they know: a new coworker, a younger relative, a friend who's just discovered something. Picture doing what Priscilla and Aquila did: not correcting them in public, but taking them aside, adding what you know, and cheering them on. Then think of who once did that for you, and if you pray, give thanks for them.
Tentmakers. Paul, Priscilla and Aquila, working with their hands, and taking a gifted preacher aside to teach him more perfectly. Today's word.
Your line: more perfectly. Tomorrow, a long sermon and an open window. Day five hundred fifty-two, done.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Saints Aquila and Priscilla, traditionally on July 8, and the Church teaches the dignity of ordinary work; many lay Catholics serve as catechists alongside their jobs.

original.note: Greek: tentmakers, the trade Paul shared with Aquila and Priscilla. some think it meant leatherworkers.

trapdoor: what you thought: Paul was a full-time preacher.
what it means: he worked with his hands alongside a married couple, who later quietly taught a famous preacher what he was missing.
what a scholar hears: the expulsion of Jews from Rome under Claudius is also mentioned by the Roman historian Suetonius. and Priscilla is named before Aquila in most mentions.

notes: Acts 18:26 quoted from the KJV because the carry 'more perfectly' follows the KJV; the Douay-Rheims reads differently (possibly 'more diligently'). Confirm whether a Douay quotation is preferred.
Priscilla named first in 4 of 6 mentions (Acts 18:18, 18:26; Romans 16:3; 2 Timothy 4:19); confirm 'most mentions' and 'many scholars think' hedge.
Feast of Aquila and Priscilla, July 8 in the Roman Martyrology; confirm.
Suetonius, Claudius 25.4 ('impulsore Chresto'): the link to Acts 18:2 is widely accepted; confirm.

Reviewer changed 'Paul later reminds churches' to the Thessalonians, since 1 Thessalonians was probably written from Corinth during this same stay (dating is debated), and 'Luke often names Priscilla first' to 'more than once' (Luke names her first in 18:18 and, in the critical text, 18:26, but Aquila first in 18:2). Note the KJV's own text of 18:26 reads 'Aquila and Priscilla'.
Myth 'Paul lived only on gifts from the churches' is false as worded, but Paul did accept gifts from Philippi (Philippians 4:15–16; 2 Corinthians 11:9). Confirm the explanation is fair.

Audit (second sample): the teach quoted the King James on the Catholic path; Acts 18:26 is now quoted from the Douay-Rheims ('more diligently'), and the carry's 'more perfectly' is explained, unquoted, as older English wording. 'One of the most gifted preachers' is replaced by Paul naming Apollos alongside himself and Peter (1 Corinthians 1:12; 3:4–6). The old note about quoting the KJV no longer applies.
